title: What game engine do ya'll use in your workflows?
author: Professional_Job_307
selftext:
Currently I don't think AI tools like Codex have any good integration with popular game engines like Godot, Unity or Unreal, so what do you guys use?

  
A custom engine is a big nono in regular gamedev so I assume this applies here too??

comments.author: Slackluster
comments.body:
Try using [LittleJS.](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS) It is a free and open source game engine works great with AI.

* [LittleJS AI Info](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/LittleJS-AI) \- Examples and tools for using AI with LittleJS.
* [LittleJS GPT](https://chatgpt.com/g/g-67c7c080b5bc81919736bc8815836be6-littlejs-game-maker) \- Make games directly in ChatGPT.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body: I don't get it, they are likely heavily utilizing AI in their development workflow, yet don't realize that providing skills with the engine would be so beneficial for other developers and users.

comments.author: NuclearStudent
comments.body:
\> A custom engine is a big nono in regular gamedev 

It all depends on who you are working for and what their needs are. If you work for a company it is likely they'll use an engine, unless it's a company so big that they're using their own custom engine. But my impression is that AI tools should work fine with Unity and so on - there should be enough training data.

comments.author: Felfedezni
comments.body: I only use FOSS so gidot.

comments.author: Former_Produce1721
comments.body: I made a custom game engine

replies.author: kauthonk
replies.body: Same, I wanted to do something a bit different

comments.author: pennystudio
comments.body:
What do you mean integration? If you mean an extension with the Godot IDE that have codex or Claude code, then sure there is none. 

But that doesn't stop you from using AI with Godot or Unity. I am personally using Claude code to build a pretty complicated Godot game. It could definitely write Godot code, and I rarely have to open up the Godot IDE.

replies.author: Both_Alternative890
replies.body: AI can't do anything helpful in Unity without MCP which currently under paywall.

comments.author: syn_krown
comments.body:
I prefer to build my own. Then I have control over every aspect.

Who says building your own is a big no no? I mean, i agree with not reinventing the wheel, but if you can build a functional game engine, then you will learn about optimization, and thats something sorely lacking in a lot of titles these days

comments.author: EnumeratedArray
comments.body:
> A custom engine is a big nono in regular gamedev

Says who? Use whatever engine you like and understand. The only person who can say an engine is wrong is you.

Personally I use Claude Code and Godot. It's very good but I find that I needed to make sure there is solid test coverage and a headless CLI which lets the AI agent "play' they game itself to test it. Otherwise I got lots of bugs and regression.

replies.author: Crawling_Hustler
replies.body: OP is saying that making ur own engine for regular gamedev is overkill or too hard unless you r making smth worldchanging in gamedev industry.  N its true

replies.author: nifft_the_lean
replies.body: Just asking the question shows that you are either a solo dev or a hobbyist. Securing funding or a publisher for a production ain't happening if you tell them you made your own engine. There's a more serious side to Game development that just vibe coding and winging it.

comments.author: Old-Moment-5297
comments.body: I use Bevy

replies.author: siendo64
replies.body: How are your build times? I was trying a workflow and it started at 45 minutes cold with just a box rendering on screen. I did a bunch of work to remove all unnecessary crates and got that to 15 minutes, but that's just insane to me.

replies.author: Old-Moment-5297
replies.body: It takes around 2 minutes for me after a code change. The editor web build is comparatively small at about 6s. I didn't do linker/cache tuning or a faster local dev profile.

comments.author: BitPsychological2767
comments.body:
>A custom engine is a big nono in regular gamedev

I don't think this is true unless you're a beginner.

comments.author: Den_er_da_hvid
comments.body: I tried using löve 2d.

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
I use github copilot coding agent, usually with claude, to develop in kotlin multiplatform / compose multiplatform for desktop (windows,  macOS, linux, anything that runs JVM), mobile (android and iOS) and web (web assembly /wasm).

So no _game_ engine.

But I have to add that I just do this as a hobby next to my daytime job as a software developer for company software.

comments.author: robogame_dev
comments.body: AI does fine with godot

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body: Makes sense - token prediction is 1d, terrible architecture for learning 2d and 3d patterns even if there was enough training data on terrains, which I doubt.

replies.author: Professional_Job_307
replies.body: I beg to differ. Check out [https://voxelbench.ai/](https://voxelbench.ai/) . I think it's clear the models are getting vastly more capable at 3d, though still a bit messy for now.

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body: That still works by generating a 1d token stream - the reason it’s so comparatively inept compared to those models’ ability at natively 1d content like writing and code is showing the point.

replies.author: Professional_Job_307
replies.body: All of our actions can be defined in a 1d token stream. similar to that of LLMs, we only generate actions in one direction: forward. We take action in 2d and 3d space using this simple output stream grom our brain, like that of LLMs.

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body:
That’s not correct. Our brain has a large parallel bundle of nerves, because their are parallel they are emitting multiple signals simultaneously. This is fundamentally different from emitting one token at a time. 

LLM = all output flows out of one wire, one steam. Human brain is nothing like that it has an enormous number of competing streams of output at once.

comments.author: proexwhy
comments.body: What do you mean when you say that current AI doesnt have good integration with popular game engines? I have been using claude with a unity mcp server and its been working like a charm. Its fails at some of the UI stuff, but honestly, Id rather be handling that myself anyways.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Godot, Unity and Unreal all have various MCPs or CLIs, or you can create your own. Godot you don't even need the MCP since all data can be manipulated directly through the files and the AI can handle both gdscript and c# fine.

You can build a custom engine too, or just build a project from scratch. Depends on what you need and your scope. Custom engines are usually overkill.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: Godot

comments.author: Aesthetic-Engine
comments.body: I created [Godot Runtime Bridge ](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/4814). My agents use it to build, test and debug in Godot and I never need to work in the editor.

comments.author: piXelicidio
comments.body: What models know about Unity because of the amount of training data is more important than integration.

comments.author: MHVANMX
comments.body: I'm using UE5 paired with a plugin I made to easily show my assets to the AI, I'm aware integrated copilots exist but they are really expensive so I prefer my own method

comments.author: SentenceProper2418
comments.body: i use stuff from Reallusion, like iClone for fast animation, Character Creator for building rigs quickly, and ActorCore for motion libraries, and then i just export everything into Unity/Unreal. This combo works pretty well for me

comments.author: Neat-Emu-8731
comments.body: I’ve been mostly staying with Unity/Unreal as the main engine since that’s still where everything plugs in cleanly, and AI tools haven’t really changed that part of the workflow yet. I also use Character creator for quickly building consistent characters, iclone for blocking/cleaning up animation fast, and Actorcore from reallusion for grabbing ready-made motion. then i just bring everything into Unity or Unreal for the actual game side. smooth setup for me.
